headline: Biman suspends Riyadh and Dammam flights over security concerns
summary: Flights to Dammam are halted until October 25 and Riyadh flights until October 31, while services to Jeddah and Medina remain operational.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended all flights from Dhaka to Dammam until October 25 and all flights to Riyadh until October 31. The airline cited security concerns as the reason for the suspension.
A flight carrying 379 passengers departed Dhaka for Dammam at 8:00 AM on Thursday, October 22, shortly before the suspension took effect.
Flights to Jeddah and Medina will continue to operate according to their scheduled timings.
Passengers traveling to Dammam and Riyadh can use Jeddah and Medina airports as alternative routes, provided seats are available.
caption:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has halted flights to Riyadh and Dammam due to security concerns.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended all flights from Dhaka to Dammam until October 25 and all flights to Riyadh until October 31. The airline cited security concerns as the reason for the suspension.

A flight carrying 379 passengers departed Dhaka for Dammam at 8:00 AM on Thursday, October 22, shortly before the suspension took effect.

Flights to Jeddah and Medina will continue to operate according to their scheduled timings.

Passengers traveling to Dammam and Riyadh can use Jeddah and Medina airports as alternative routes, provided seats are available.

headline_marked: 2 [[Bangladeshis injured in attack]] on Saudi airport
headline: 2 Bangladeshis injured in attack on Saudi airport
summary: Two expatriates from Cumilla and Noakhali were injured in a strike targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
details: Two Bangladeshi expatriates were injured in an attack targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia.
The injured Bangladeshis have been identified as Sajal Chandra Das from Cumilla and Mohammad Abdur Rahim from Noakhali.
According to the expatriates’ welfare ministry, both are currently receiving treatment at the Saudi German Hospital in Dammam.
The attack, which occurred on Wednesday night, also left two Indian nationals dead and eight others injured.
Among the injured are two Indians, two Yemenis, one Saudi national, and one Nepali.
Several of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis injured in a deadly attack on a Saudi airport.

Two Bangladeshi expatriates were injured in an attack targeting King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia.

The injured Bangladeshis have been identified as Sajal Chandra Das from Cumilla and Mohammad Abdur Rahim from Noakhali.

According to the expatriates’ welfare ministry, both are currently receiving treatment at the Saudi German Hospital in Dammam.

The attack, which occurred on Wednesday night, also left two Indian nationals dead and eight others injured.

Among the injured are two Indians, two Yemenis, one Saudi national, and one Nepali.

Several of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.
